description: This bar chart illustrates the number of samples for various input and output configurations, with the vertical axis labeled "Number" and scaled linearly from 0 to 120,000, and the horizontal axis displaying six distinct categories corresponding to different input/output sizes. Each category contains two bars, one for input and one for output, distinguished by color and pattern as indicated in the legend: yellow with diagonal stripes for "2K-Input", salmon with diagonal stripes for "4K-Input", light blue with diagonal stripes for "8K-Input", dark blue with diagonal stripes for "16K-Input", yellow with diagonal stripes for "2K-Output", salmon with diagonal stripes for "4K-Output", light blue with diagonal stripes for "8K-Output", and dark blue with diagonal stripes for "16K-Output". The bars are arranged horizontally from left to right in the order of increasing input size (2K, 4K, 8K, 16K), and within each group, the input bar is positioned to the left of the output bar. The values for each bar are explicitly labeled on top: the "2K-Input" bar is 9,320, the "2K-Output" bar is 78,188; the "4K-Input" bar is 3,784, the "4K-Output" bar is 108,494; the "8K-Input" bar is 1,401, the "8K-Output" bar is 17,865; and the "16K-Input" bar is 832, the "16K-Output" bar is 4,247. The bars are not sorted by value but are presented in the order of increasing input size. There is no visual emphasis such as shading, bolding, or outlining applied to any specific bar.
